prompt.context: Sparkle Co. is a mid-sized private beverage company ($900MM annual sales) that manufactures sparkling water in a range of flavors. After several years of profitable growth, Sparkle Co. has seen profitability deteriorate in the past year. The CEO dreams about taking the company public, and has hired our firm to diagnose the problem and help turn things around.
prompt.question: What is wrong with profitability and how can the client turn things around?

clarifying_info.q: Do you have any figures on revenues or costs?
clarifying_info.a: We don't have any figures yet about revenues or costs — we just know net profit is down slightly vs. last year.

clarifying_info.q: Where does Sparkle Co. operate and sell?
clarifying_info.a: Sparkle Co. is based in New York City and sells across the country through retailers such as grocery stores and drugstores, and major ecommerce sites like amazon.com.
They do not want to expand outside the US.

exhibits.title: Sparkling Water Market Size in the United States
exhibits.shows: Bar chart showing US sparkling water market size in billions of USD from 2014 to 2018

exhibits.title: Sparkle Co. P&L (in USD Millions)
exhibits.shows: Income statement for Sparkle Co. from 2014 to 2018 showing total revenue, gross margin %, R&D expense, SG&A expense, and net profit

exhibits.title: Sparkle Co. Customer Survey Results
exhibits.shows: Two-part customer survey: (1) importance rating (1-5) of purchase factors; (2) Sparkle Co. performance rating (1-5) on each factor. Factors include healthiness, visual appearance/packaging, taste, variety of flavors, price, and availability.
exhibits.data: Survey scores for importance vs. performance across 6 purchase factors

exhibits.title: Functional Beverages Market Size in the United States
exhibits.shows: Bar chart showing projected US functional beverages market size in billions of USD for 2020, 2021, and 2022, with Sparkle Co. projected market share annotations of 1%, 3%, and 5%

framework: Profitability: Revenue (price — wholesale & retail, promotions/discounts; units sold) and Costs (variable — unit cost, transportation, manufacturing; fixed — manufacturing & production, marketing/sales)
Market: Competition (multinationals, new entrants); Customers — consumers (health trends, interest/demand, purchase behaviors, segments) and retailers (shelf space, bargaining power)
Company: Products (is a particular product line doing poorly?); Sales Channels (is a particular channel doing poorly?); Marketing (change in tactics/channels); People (turnover, cultural issues)

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1 and Exhibit 2, what can you conclude about the company's profitability issues? What has happened to Sparkle Co.'s market share?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify: (1) The overall market grew ~9% from 2017 to 2018, but Sparkle Co. revenue fell ~3.75% ($935M to $900M), meaning they are losing market share. (2) Gross margin has been flat at 25%, so COGs has not changed. (3) R&D and SG&A are both down YoY, meaning fixed costs are declining — possibly due to reduced investment in product innovation. Conclusion: declining profitability is a revenue/market-share problem, not a cost problem. Candidate should brainstorm reasons: competition (new entrants, increased marketing, private label), distribution (reduced shelf space, lost accounts), customer perception shift, or product/quality issues.

math.setup: Calculate Sparkle Co. market share each year using Exhibit 1 (market size) and Exhibit 2 (revenue). Market share = Sparkle Co. Revenue / Total Market Size.
math.answer: Market share was 15% in 2014, rose to a peak of 17% in 2016-2017, and has now fallen back to 15% in 2018, confirming Sparkle Co. is losing share in a growing market.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 3, what can you conclude from the customer research? What would you recommend?
questions.guidance: From the survey, candidates should identify: (1) Sparkle Co. is underperforming customer expectations on healthiness and visual appearance/packaging — indicating an opportunity to redesign packaging and improve health perception. (2) Sparkle Co. exceeds expectations on price — indicating possible room to raise prices or launch a premium product. Recommended actions: packaging redesign; marketing campaign emphasizing health benefits/low calorie/no sugar; launch a new 'healthy' beverage line at a higher price point; partnerships with health influencers, doctors, or nutritionists; revamp social media and website.

questions.prompt: The R&D team has developed a functional beverages line (CBD, turmeric, collagen, spirulina, etc.) that could launch in 2020. Evaluate the opportunity using Exhibit 4 and the following cost data: upfront fixed costs of $40MM ($10MM finish product development, $30MM additional production capacity); annual fixed costs of $8MM/year; gross margin of 30%.
questions.guidance: Candidate should: (1) Note the $10MM development cost is sunk in spirit but provided as an upfront cash outlay to complete. (2) Calculate 3-year P&L using projected revenue and given margins. (3) Note breakeven occurs between Year 2 and Year 3 (relatively fast). (4) Note the 30% gross margin is higher than the 25% on the core product. (5) Optionally note that total 3-year revenue of $310MM is still small relative to the $900MM core business.

math.setup: Year 1: market ~$1.5B × 1% share = $15M... (use given revenue figures from exhibit). Given: Revenue Y1=$20M, Y2=$90M, Y3=$200M; GM=30%; Annual fixed costs=$8M; Upfront costs=$40M.
steps: Year 1: Gross Profit = $20M × 30% = $6M; Net after fixed costs = $6M - $8M = -$2M
Year 2: Gross Profit = $90M × 30% = $27M; Net after fixed costs = $27M - $8M = +$19M
Year 3: Gross Profit = $200M × 30% = $60M; Net after fixed costs = $60M - $8M = +$52M
Upfront costs = $40M; 3-year net = $69M - $40M = +$29M profit over 3 years

Breakeven: Upfront $40M is recovered between Year 2 and Year 3 (after Year 2 cumulative = -$2M + $19M = +$17M; still $23M short of covering $40M upfront; by end of Year 3 cumulative = +$69M, well past breakeven)
math.answer: 3-year cumulative net profit (after upfront costs) = +$29M. Breakeven on upfront investment is reached during Year 3.

brainstorming.prompt: What are potential reasons Sparkle Co. is losing market share in a growing sparkling water market?

categories.name: Competition
ideas: New entrants offering similar or differentiated products
Private label competitors gaining shelf space

categories.name: Distribution
ideas: Reduced shelf space at key retailers
Missing new distribution channels (e.g., convenience stores, gyms)

categories.name: Customer
ideas: Shift in consumer preference toward healthier or functional beverages
Changed perception of Sparkle Co. brand
Preference for other flavors or formats

categories.name: Product
ideas: Insufficient product innovation or new SKUs
Packaging perceived as outdated or unhealthy
Inadequate marketing spend on brand awareness

recommendation: Launch the functional beverages line: it addresses customer demand for healthier options, targets a high-growth market, generates higher gross margins (30% vs. 25%), and reaches breakeven within approximately 2-3 years

Alternatively, do not launch: breakeven is still 2+ years away, does not address the immediate decline in the core business, and the new product line is relatively small compared to the $900MM core business
risks: If revenue projections are wrong or overstated, the investment could be unprofitable
Entering a new category introduces new competitors and potentially draws management focus from the core business
Health ingredient regulations (CBD, collagen, etc.) may create compliance risk or product restrictions
Capital allocated to new product could alternatively be reinvested in the core sparkling water business
next_steps: Re-evaluate revenue projections to assess whether the 1%/3%/5% market share assumptions are realistic
Evaluate parallel actions to improve the core sparkling water business (packaging redesign, marketing, price adjustments) while pursuing the new product launch
